  LOUISIANA ENERGY SERVICES, LLC's AND FEDERAL EXECUTIVE AGENCIES'
          EXCEPTIONS TO THE CERTIFICATION OF STIPULATION

        Intervenors Louisiana Energy Services ("LES") and the Federal Executive Agencies

 ("FEA") hereby jointly submit to the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission ("Commission"

 or "NMPRC") their Exceptions to the Certification of Stipulation ("Certification") pursuant to

 1.2.2.20(B)(5)(b) NMAC. LES and FEA are signatories to the Stipulation that was filed on June

 22, 2026 following extensive negotiations in which all parties were invited to participate

 (“Stipulation”). The only party that opposed any portion of the Stipulation was the Commission's

 Utility Division Staff ("Staff"). All other parties either joined the Stipulation or did not oppose it.

        LES and FEA are in agreement with the majority of the Certification, which largely

 recommends approval of the Stipulation. LES's and FEA’s exceptions pertain to two of the

 Certification's proposed modifications to the Stipulation enumerated in Section IV, Findings and

 Conclusions, Subsection 9 (pp. 150 – 153): Modifications to the Stipulation.

        In Subsection 9, on page 150, the Certification states that:

        The following provisions are the product of serious negotiation but must be
        modified to produce fair, just, and reasonable rates that are in the public interest
        and consistent with important Commission rules and practice.
        For the reasons explained below, LES and FEA do not agree that two of the proposed

 modifications are in the public interest or that they are consistent with important Commission rules
 and practice. In addition, LES and FEA recommend that, in the event the Commission adopts

modifications to the Stipulation, it also provides time to obtain signatories' positions on the

modifications and whether they withdraw from the Stipulation.

LES/FEA Exception No. 1: The System Load Factor Used for Class Allocation of Production
and Transmission Costs as Set Forth in the Stipulation Should Not be Amended.

        The Certification at Section IV Subsection 9.i.e., page 152, finds and concludes that:
        SPS shall allocate among rate classes all costs of production and transmission,
        including Hale and Sagamore wind generation, on an AED 4-CP basis. The system
        load factor method should use AED 4-CP, not the 1-CP.
        LES and FEA except to this finding and conclusion and the corresponding recommended

Decretal Paragraph B on page 154. No witness testified that adoption of the stipulated 1-CP

methodology would result in unjust, unreasonable, or discriminatory rates. Moreover, every party,

including Staff, supported the use of 1-CP methodology for the system load factor.1 The

Certification fails to provide rationale to reject the use of 1-CP and the Staff’s position on this

issue is not supported by the evidentiary record. The Certification fails to establish how the

proposed change to a provision agreed to by all parties is in the public interest and consistent with

important Commission rules and practice.

        The Certification appears to be concerned that acceptance of this provision would

somehow adversely affect the parties' and the Commission's ability to proceed with workshops on

cost allocation that were agreed to in the stipulation approved in Case No. 25-00085-UT. To the

contrary, this provision of the Stipulation in this case in no way precludes or predetermines any

future workshops on cost allocation issues or otherwise amends or supersedes the stipulation




1
  See Direct Testimony of Larry Blank at 14:12-19; see also Settlement Testimony of Michael P. Gorman
at 7:12-8:6 testifying (that it is appropriate to allocate the portfolio within retail class cost of service using
an Average and Excess Four Coincident Peak (“A&E 4CP”) methodology that has been used in past rate
cases to allocate SPS resource portfolio costs).
                                                        2
 approved in Case No. 25-00082-UT.2 As a Stipulation, the provisions do not apply as precedent

for any future Commission decision.3

        Further, the proposed modification fails to take into account that this provision was an

important element of the give and take of settlement negotiations and the overall result agreed to

by the signatories, which represent a diverse array of interests. This modification would harm the

outcome that signatories negotiated, and fails to take into account concessions that signatories

made, including the application of gradualism to benefit residential customers.

LES/FEA Exception No. 2: The Stipulation’s Proposed Allocation of Production Credits
Should Not Be Changed
        The Certification at Section IV Subsection 9.e.iii at page 153 finds and concludes that:
        PTCs should be allocated with the AED 4-CP allocator, not the stipulated Energy-
        at-Source Allocator.
        LES and FEA except to this finding and conclusion, and to the corresponding

recommended Decretal Paragraph B on page 154. The Certification identifies no evidentiary or

policy basis for modifying the Stipulation's agreed-upon allocation of PTCs, and in fact provides

no rationale for this modification to the Stipulation. The Energy-at-Source allocation of production

tax credits ("PTCs") is reasonable and fair because PTCs are energy-related elements whose costs

and benefits flow to customers through the fuel clause.4 The Energy-at-Source allocation reflects

how these energy-related PTCs are produced, and allocates PTC benefits consistent with each unit

of energy attributable to a class.5

        As with the proposed modification discussed above, this change would alter a material

component of the negotiated settlement and undermine the balance of compromises reached by


2
  See Stipulation at Section 1.11.
3
  1.2.2.20(D) NMAC (“Unless the commission explicitly provides otherwise in the order approving the
stipulation, approval of a stipulation does not constitute commission approval of or precedent regarding any
principle or issue in the proceeding”).
4
  See Settlement Testimony of Michael P. Gorman at 6:18 through 7:4.
5
  Tr. Vol 2 (Trowbridge) at 464:9-14.
                                                     3
 the signatories, and would fail to take into account concessions that signatories made, including

application of gradualism to benefit residential customers. If the Commission accepts this

proposed modification, it should apply only to the PTCs associated with the resources at issue in

this proceeding, not PTCs associated with Hale and Sagamore generation that were not at issue

or addressed within the scope of this case.6

LES/FEA Exception No. 3: The Certification of Stipulation Does Not Provide a Mechanism
for Stipulation Signatories to Withdraw if the Stipulation is Modified.
       The Certification does not provide signatories the opportunity to accept or not accept the

recommended modifications in Section IV Subsection 9.e, or to withdraw from the Stipulation in

the event the Commission accepts and adopts any of the Certification's proposed modifications to

the Stipulation that signatories find unacceptable. Fundamental fairness requires that parties be

afforded an opportunity to determine whether they remain willing to support a settlement after

material modifications are imposed. If the Commission does accept and adopt the Certification's

proposed modifications to the Stipulation, the Commission should provide in its order a reasonable

time frame for each signatory to notify the Commission whether it accepts or rejects the

modification(s)) and whether it elects to withdraw from the Stipulation in light of the

modifications. In the event one or more of the signatories do not accept the modifications or

withdraw from the Stipulation, the Commission should provide a reasonable time frame to obtain

input from parties and to determine how to proceed with this case in light of that development as

well as the current 11-month suspension period that ends on November 30, 2026, including time

for a new hearing on SPS's application and parties' direct and rebuttal testimonies, rather than on

the Stipulation that was the subject of the July 2026 hearing.



6
 See In re Commission’s Investigation of Rates for Gas Serv. of PNM’s Gas Servs., 2000-NMSC-008, ¶14,
128 N.M. 747, 998 P.2d 1198 (reversing the Commission’s decision on rate design for lack of substantial
evidence).
                                                  4
        Wherefore, LES and FEA respectfully request the Commission reject the Certification's

recommended modifications discussed herein and instead accept and approve the Stipulation as it

was agreed to by the signatories or with the other proposed recommended modifications to which

signatories do not except. In the event the Commission modifies the Stipulation provisions, it

should provide a reasonable time frame to obtain input from parties and to determine how to

proceed with this case, including time for a new hearing on SPS's application and parties' direct

and rebuttal testimonies, rather than on the Stipulation that was the subject of the July 2026

hearing.

Respectfully submitted on November 2, 2026,
